(a) spike synchronization is possible in networks of silicon integrate-and fire neurons despite their inherent fabrication related variance, (b) spike synchronization is obtained by lateral excitation between neurons in the network, and global inhibition, and (c) this behavior is similar to that obtained from networks of biological neurons.
spike synchronization can be obtained from simple networks of VLSI integrate-and-fire neurons interconnected by lateral and global connections.
a network of VLSi integrate-and-fire neurons with lateral excitation and inhibition can be synchronized by the application of a common stimulus.

the study of spiking neural networks for real-time event-based computing, using VLSI hardware implementations of neurons.
the design of VLSI neuronal networks that can be used to study event-based processing in the brain, and to develop new computational models based on such networks.
the study of spatio-temporally distributed neuronal mechanisms in the context of event-based computation.
